question: As of October 2022, in which of the following Harappan cities was the Citadel NOT walled off ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lothal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lothal is one of the most prominent cities of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization, located in the Bhal region of the modern state of Gujarat.
 
• Unlike other major Harappan cities, the Citadel in Lothal was not walled off, which is unique compared to the cities like Harappa, Kalibangan, and Mohenjo-Daro.
 
• Lothal was a vital and thriving trade center, and its dockyard was one of the world's earliest known, indicating its significance in maritime trade.
 
• The city layout of Lothal includes well-planned residential areas, a marketplace, and a vast dock which signifies advanced urban planning and engineering skills.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Harappa**

 
 
• Harappa is one of the major cities of the Indus Valley Civilization, located in present-day Pakistan.
 
• It had a fortified Citadel, which was an elevated area used for administrative and religious purposes.
 
• The city was well-planned with advanced drainage systems, granaries, and standardized weights and measures.
 
 
 
• **Kalibangan**
 
 
• Kalibangan is located in present-day Rajasthan, India.
 
• It had a distinct walled Citadel and lower town, showcasing the typical Harappan city layout.
 
• Archaeological findings include fire altars, which suggest the practice of ritualistic activities.
 
 
 
• **Mohenjo-Daro**
 
 
• Mohenjo-Daro, located in present-day Sindh, Pakistan, is one of the largest cities of the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• The Citadel at Mohenjo-Daro was also fortified, indicating a separate administrative and possibly religious area.
 
• It is famous for the Great Bath, a large public water tank, and advanced urban infrastructure.
